sentences.text: Wife and mother of deceased Varadaraju K. filed petition under Section 166 of IMV Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.80,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owner and insurer of the Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 alleging that on 07.10.2023 at 7.00 a.m. when Varadaraju riding Honda Activa bearing No.KA-41-EU-0560 from Channarayapattana towards Bengaluru, near Byaladakere gate on NH-75 within the limits of Amruthur police station, driver of Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 drove the same negligently from Yadiyur towards Bangalore, dashed the same to hind part of Honda Activa, thereby caused the accident, caused grievous injuries to Varadaraju.

Immediately after accident, Varadaraju has been shifted to Govt. Hospital, Kunigal,
wherein first aid has been provided, then shifted to Bengaluru, however, on the way of Bengaluru hospital, succumbed to the injuries.

2. As on the date of accident deceased Varadaraju being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.3,000/- per day by maintaining mobile street hotel and catering at Rajarajeswari Nagara,
Bengaluru.

3. Regarding accident Amruthur police registered a case in crime No.153/2023 against the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958.
4.
Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.1 owner of Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 remained absent.

5. In response to the notice respondent No.2, Insurance Company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason and mode of accident, age,
occupation and income of the deceased.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 27.07.2024, this Authority has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 07.10.2023 at about 07.00 a.m., on Bengaluru - Mangalore NH-75, near Byaladakere gate, Amruthur Hobli, Tumkur district, in view of the negligent use of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-07-A-9958 accident taken place resulting in the death of Varadaraju K., S/o.Kumar Shetty?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

7. On 27.07.2024, 08.08.2024, petitioner No.1- Sunitha deposed as P.W.1 and produced 15 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.15.
During cross-examination of P.W.1, learned Advocate appearing for the Insurance Company get marked copy of Learner Licence of Varadaraju at Ex.R.1.
On 23.10.2024 petitioners produced evidence of Nagaraju, S/o.Nanjundaiah as P.W.2.

On 03.12.2024 Insurance Company produced the evidence of Officer as R.W.1 and produced 2 documents at Ex.R.2 and R.3.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

9. On the basis of material on record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative; Issue No.2 ... Petitioners are entitle to receive Rs.28,09,120/- with current and future interest at 6%p..a. from the respondents as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

REASONS 10. Issue No.1:-
In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No.2 - Insurance Company

by analyzing the evidence available in the file requested to answer Issue No.1 in favour of the Insurance Company on the ground that as on the date of alleged accident, Varadaraju had Learner Licence to ride Honda Activa by relying on the following judgments:
1. AIR 1996 SC 1150 Civil Appeal No.3486/1986 (New India Assurance Co.Ltd. -Vs- Mandar Madhav Tambe and Others).
2. AIR 2011 SC 3547, SLP No.24020/2011 with 24021- 24023/2011 (Alka Ojha -Vs- Rajasthan Public Service Commission and Another).
3. ACJ 2005 1968, High Court of Delhi (Rama Nand Pandey and others -Vs- Nisha Tiwari and others).

11. In the lengthy argument, learned Advocate appearing for petitioners by analyzing the evidence available on file, requested to answer Issue No.1 in favour of petitioners on the ground that negligent driving of the Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 was the reason for the accident.

In the evidence affidavit P.W.2 - Nagaraju, S/o Nanjundaiah stated that on 07.10.2023 at 7.00 p.m. when he was riding Bike from Yadiyur towards Kunigal, in front of his Bike, a rider of Honda Activa by wearing helmet proceeding towards Bengaluru, at the same time driver of Tanker Lorry drove the same negligently from Mangalore towards Bengaluru dashed the same to Honda Activa,
therefore, the rider of Honda Activa along with Honda Activa fell on left side of the road and suffered grievous injuries, immediately himself and public went to spot, noticed the registration number of Honda Activa and Lorry as KA-07-A-9958 and KA-41-EU-0560, immediately shifted the injured to the Govt.Hospital, Kunigal, he intimated the incident to Manjunath, brother of the injured through the mobile of the injured, then relatives of the injured, shifted to Bengaluru, then came to know that on the way of Bengaluru hospital at 8.45 p.m. near Nelamangala bypass succumbed to the injuries.
P.W.2 stated that Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 was the reason for the accident.
17. In the cross-examination P.W.2 stated about non filing of the complaint about the accident.

18. In the evidence affidavit R.W.1 - Officer of Insurance Company stated that rider of Honda Activa has no valid Driving Licence at the time of accident, however, the rider of the Honda Activa had only LLR.

21. In this case, there are no reasons to disbelieve the contents of police records and oral evidence of P.W.2 - Nagaraju, S/o.Nanjundaiah regarding reason and mode of accident.

According to law, for the time being in force, irrespective of nature of driving licence possessed by two wheeler rider,
driver of Tanker Lorry is bound to drive the Lorry cautiously and carefully.

22. Hence, I have concluded that on 07.10.2023 at 7.00 a.m., when Varadaraju riding Honda Activa bearing No.KA-41-EU-0560 from Channarayapattana towards Bengaluru, on NH-75, near Byaladakere gate within the limits of Amruthur police station, Chandregowda, S/o.

Shivegowda negligently drove the Lorry bearing No.KA- 07-A-9958 from Yadiyur side towards Bangalore,
dashed the same to Honda Activa, thereby caused the accident, caused the death of Varadaraju.
Hence, I answer issue No. 1 in the Affirmative.
23. Issue No.2:

In the evidence P.W.1 stated that as on the date of accident, her husband Varadaraju being aged about 35 years, used to earn Rs.3,000/- per day by maintaining street hotel at Rajarajeshwari Nagar, Bengaluru and doing catering business and used to contribute entire income to the family.
24. In the written statement respondent No.2 Insurance Company denied the allegation regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased Varadaraju.

25. In the cross-examination, P.W.1 denied the suggestion that as on the date of accident her husband never earning Rs.3,000/- per day by doing catering and street hotel business at Rajarajeshwari Nagar, Bengaluru.
26. In the evidence P.W.2-Nagaraju S/o.Nanjundaiah and R.W.1-Officer of Insurance company stated nothing regarding age, occupation and income of the deceased.
27. In the P.M. Report, Inquest Mahazar, age of Varadaraju is noted as 39 years.

In the copy of the Aadhar card and Learner's Licence marked at Ex.P.14 and Ex.R.1, date of birth of Varadaraju is noted as 01.01.1985.
28.
Ex.P.12 is the Food Safety Supervisor Certificate of Competence issued by Food safety and Standards Authority of India to Varadaraju on 22.06.2022.

Hence, I have inferred that, it is fit and proper to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency presuming that as on the date of incident Varadaraju being aged about 38 years, used to earn approximately Rs.16,000/- p.m. by maintaining catering business and doing street food business in Rajarajeshawari Nagar, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: Add : 40% towards future prospects - Rs.22,400/- (16,000/- + 6,400/-)
Less : 1/3rd towards personal expenses of - Rs.14,934/- the deceased Varadaraju (22,400/- - 7,466/- = 14,934/-)

Annual income of the deceased 14,934/- x12 - Rs.1,79,208/-
 Multiplier Applicable - 15  Loss of dependency 1,79,208/-x15 - Rs.26,88,120/-
31.

Hence, I award Rs.26,88,120/- towards loss of dependency, Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate, Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.88,000/-
towards loss of consortium to petitioners No.1 and 2 at the rate of Rs.44,000/- each.

32. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioners being wife and mother of deceased Varadaraju are entitle to receive Rs.28,09,120/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. as compensation from the respondents.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly.
33. Issue No.3:
Copy of the policy marked at Ex.R.3 shows that as on the date of incident, Lorry had insurance coverage with respondent No.2.
In the file there are no evidence to show that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 owner of the Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA- 07-A-9958 has violated any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the owner and insurer of Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A- 9958 are liable to pay compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents No.1 and 2 to pay compensation to the petitioners,

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :

sentences.text: The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.

The respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.28,09,120/- (Rupees Twenty eight lakhs nine thousand one hundred and twenty only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioners towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Tanker Lorry bearing No.KA-07-A-9958 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
The compensation amount and interest are distributed among petitioners equally .

After deposit of the compensation amount, 75% of the compensation amount and interest allotted in favour of petitioners may be released by crediting the same to their respective bank accounts directly.
Surplus compensation amount with interest allotted to petitioners shall be deposited in any bank in the name of the petitioners for a period of 2 years without permitting to create any encumbrances.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer-I, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 13th day of February, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T. Bangalore.
